The ATTEND study collects clinical records, radiology imaging, IHC, and WES-derived
genomic features (TMB, MSI, HRD, aneuploidy, and a per-variant MAF) on the **same
patients**. These reports link the modalities onto a shared patient ID, assemble a
per-patient master table, and analyse it.

**There is no build order.** The join lives in code/build_master.R, and every report
calls get_master(), which reads the master table when it exists and builds it when it
does not. Any report can be the first one knitted, and wflow_build() with no arguments
is always correct.

Each report opens with a four-line scope contract: the question, the cohort, what it
reads, and what it deliberately leaves to another report. They are numbered in reading
order, 00 to 09.

**[00 — Methods](00-methods.html)** carries every justification in the pipeline, and the
shared definitions each report links to rather than repeating: the two TMB definitions, the
aneuploidy classes, what "MMR-deficient only" means, the highlight groups, and how the
master is built. Operational recipes — running GISTIC on the cluster, classification
alternatives — live in runbooks/.

### Build

- **[01 — Data integration](01-data-integration.html)** · all patients
  Part 1 translates three ID spaces onto one patient key, collapses each modality to one
  row per patient, and writes the master. Part 2 audits what that cost: unmapped records,
  coverage per dataset, the UpSet of who has which modality, and value sanity.

### QC and validation

- **[02 — FlowPath vs the pathologist](02-flowpath-concordance.html)** · all imaged
  Does the automated quantification agree with the pathologist's eye, on continuous
  measures and categorical calls.
- **[03 — Covariate distributions by MMR status](03-covariates-by-mmr.html)** · all patients
  ECDF and Kolmogorov–Smirnov per continuous covariate, plus the aneuploidy score itself
  contrasted between MMR-deficient and -proficient tumours.

### Findings

- **[04 — Survival](04-survival.html)** · all patients
  Every Kaplan–Meier and Cox model in the pipeline: treatment arm within panels defined by
  aneuploidy × MMR, then TMB, HRD, MSI, and immune content.
- **[05 — Aneuploidy in MMR-deficient tumours](05-aneuploidy-mmrd.html)** · MMRd only
  Part 1 takes aneuploidy against mutation status, one gene at a time. Part 2 takes it
  against cell-type composition under three normalizations.
- **[06 — Treatment response and cell-type composition](06-response.html)** · all patients + MMRd
  The composition panels of report 05 Part 2, re-keyed on treatment response — a 6-month
  landmark on the survival endpoint, with patients censored before the landmark reported as
  unclassifiable rather than counted as failures. Every figure is drawn for the whole cohort
  and for the MMR-deficient stratum, and one interaction model tests whether they differ.
- **[07 — Mutation landscape and copy number](07-mutation-and-cna.html)** · all patients
  Part 1 oncoplots and the TCGA Fig. 2d subgroup frequency comparison. Part 2 recurrent
  copy number at arm and genome-wide resolution. Part 3 the aneuploidy × MMR peak contrast.
- **[08 — Tumour mutational burden](08-tmb.html)** · all patients
  Part 1 asks whether TMB resolves the hypermutator population as a genuine second mode.
  Part 2 draws TMB by aneuploidy once per MMR stratum. Part 3 replicates the whole battery
  in TCGA UCEC, which is tumour-normal paired.

### External

- **[09 — TCGA integrated classification](09-tcga-classification.html)** · all patients
  Reproduces the TCGA endometrial cascade (Kandoth et al. 2013), clustering GISTIC
  thresholded peaks with 1 − Pearson distance and Ward.D2 linkage and sweeping k = 2–8 on
  one chromosome heatmap. The serous-like call is directional; the undirected call is
  printed alongside and [DISAGREE] flagged when they differ.

### Conventions

Shared definitions are written **once**, in [00-methods](00-methods.html), and linked from
the reports that use them rather than rendered into each one. Reports show derivations and
results, and carry no takeaway or interpretation sections: conclusions belong in the
manuscript, where they can be revised as the data changes.

Every chunk that produces a figure or table is preceded by a derivation note saying what is
shown, where it comes from in the raw data, and which operations change its interpretation.

code/tests/test_rmd_style.R enforces the structure and code/tests/test_rmd_parse.R
checks every chunk parses. Both are base R, so they run without tidyverse or the cohort.

### Configuration lives in one place

- code/build_master.R — the join, the crosswalk assembly, and get_master().
- code/attend_harmonise.R — ID spaces, the two crosswalks, the collapse-to-patient rule.
- code/attend_classes.R — column names (attend_cols), thresholds, class derivation,
  gene panels, the TMB definitions and labels, and the CNV/TCGA-cascade config.
- code/attend_plots.R — the one palette (Tol vibrant), attend_theme(), attend_box(),
  and the highlight overlay with its crosswalk-aware id resolution.
- code/attend_ihc.R — FlowPath IHC metric definitions (reports 02, 04, 05, 06).
- code/attend_scna.R — GISTIC peak union, panel score, permutation and LOO stability.
- code/attend_bimodality.R — tmb_long(), tmb_battery(), and the bimodality measures.
